column1: Rowstore storage groups data by {{c1::row}} rather than by column.
column2:
Columns belonging to a row are stored together.
Review source

column1: Disk-based rowstore indexes use a {{c1::B+ tree}} structure.
column2:
This statement does not describe columnstore or memory-optimized indexes.
Review source

column1: A SQL Server table can have at most {{c1::one}} clustered index.
column2:
The clustered index defines the table's primary storage structure.
Review source

column1: A disk-based rowstore table without a clustered index is a {{c1::heap}}.
column2:
Its data rows do not have a clustered key order.
Review source

column1: On a clustered rowstore table, a nonclustered index uses the {{c1::clustered index key}} as its row locator.
column2:
On a heap, the locator instead points to the row's physical location.
Review source

column1: Included nonkey columns are stored at the {{c1::leaf}} level of a nonclustered rowstore index.
column2:
They add data for query coverage without becoming index key columns.
Review source

column1: To create a clustered rowstore index, use CREATE {{c1::CLUSTERED}} INDEX IX_Product_ID ON dbo.Product(ProductID);
column2:
The table must not already have another clustered index.
Review source

column1: To create a nonclustered rowstore index, use CREATE {{c1::NONCLUSTERED}} INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product(Category);
column2:
A table can have multiple nonclustered indexes for different access patterns.
Review source

column1: Add nonkey output columns with CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product(Category) {{c1::INCLUDE}} (ProductName, Price);
column2:
Category is the index key, while ProductName and Price are included columns.
Review source

column1: The data for one column within one columnstore rowgroup forms a {{c1::column segment}}.
column2:
Each segment is compressed independently.
Review source

column1: A full delta rowgroup normally closes at {{c1::1,048,576}} rows.
column2:
This is also the maximum columnstore rowgroup size, not the bulk-load minimum.
Review source

column1: For a clustered columnstore bulk load, a batch needs at least {{c1::102,400}} rows to load directly into compressed rowgroups.
column2:
Apply the threshold within each partition, and smaller leftover groups go to the deltastore.
Review source

column1: A delta rowgroup that still accepts new rows has state_desc = {{c1::OPEN}}.
column2:
It remains in rowstore format until compressed.
Review source

column1: A full delta rowgroup waiting for tuple-mover compression has state_desc = {{c1::CLOSED}}.
column2:
CLOSED does not mean that its data is already stored in compressed columnar format.
Review source

column1: A rowgroup stored in compressed columnar format has state_desc = {{c1::COMPRESSED}}.
column2:
This state differs from the OPEN and CLOSED states of delta rowgroups.
Review source

column1: On an eligible heap table, create its primary columnstore storage with CREATE {{c1::CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE}} INDEX CCI_Sales ON dbo.Sales;
column2:
A clustered columnstore index stores all table columns without a column list in this statement.
Review source

column1: Add a secondary columnstore copy with CREATE {{c1::NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE}} INDEX NCCI_Sales ON dbo.Sales(Amount, Quantity);
column2:
The column list selects the columns copied into the index.
Review source

column1: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::total_rows}} includes rows marked deleted in a compressed rowgroup.
column2:
It counts physically stored rows rather than only currently visible rows.
Review source

column1: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::deleted_rows}} counts rows marked for deletion within a compressed clustered columnstore rowgroup.
column2:
These rows still occupy compressed storage until cleanup.
Review source

column1: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::size_in_bytes}} reports the combined page size for a rowgroup.
column2:
This excludes storage for metadata and shared dictionaries.
Review source
